problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=(2x+{y}^{2})\,i+y{e}^{x}\,j.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $F$ at the point $(1,1).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Curl of a Vector Field

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Scalar Curl of a Vector Field
examples.problem: Consider the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y) = e^{x+y} \, \mathbf{i} + 3xy \, \mathbf{j}.$ Evaluate the scalar curl of $\mathbf{F}$ at the point $(-1,1).$
examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{F} = P\,\mathbf{i} + Q\,\mathbf{j}$ is a vector field on $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $\mathbf F$ all exist, then the *scalar* curl of $\mathbf{F}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3xy)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y}) \\  & =3y-{e}^{x+y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the scalar curl at the point $(-1,1),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})}_{(-1,1)} & =3(1)-{e}^{-1+1} \\  & =3-{e}^{0} \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the curl of $F$ is the vector field given by

$$
curl\,F=∇\times F=|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ P & Q & R\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 3{z}^{2} & 2y & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(3{z}^{2})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{z}^{2})]k \\  & =(0-0)i-(0-6z)j+(0-0)k \\  & =6z\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
